'''Ouyang Ziyuan''' ({{zh|s= 欧阳自远|t=歐陽自遠|p=Ōuyáng Zìyuǎn}}, born October 9, 1935) is a Chinese [[cosmochemist]], [[geochemist]] and space advocate. He is a research professor at the Institute of Geochemistry of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=Astronautix>{{cite web|url=http://www.astronautix.com/astros/ouyiyuan.htm|title=Ouyang Ziyuan|publisher=Astronautix.com|access-date=July 10, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015001912/http://www.astronautix.com/astros/ouyiyuan.htm|archive-date=October 15, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Asteroid [[8919 Ouyangziyuan]], discovered in 1996, was named in his honor.

== Career ==
Ouyang was born in 1935 in [[Ji'an]], [[Jiangxi]].<ref name=Astronautix/> He obtained a degree in [[geology]] at the Beijing College of Geology and a [[doctorate]] in mineral deposits and geochemistry at the [[China University of Geosciences (Beijing)|Beijing Institute of Geology]].<ref name=Astronautix/> Thereafter, Ouyang spent many years conducting studies in deep [[mining|mine]]s. He later studied [[nuclear physics]] and worked in a [[particle accelerator]] laboratory. He later put forward a hypothesis on the formation of [[iron meteorite]]s, an evolutionary model of the formation of the meteorites which fell at [[Jilin]] in 1976, and a theory of multi-stage [[cosmic ray]] radiation history.<ref name=Astronautix/> His works include ''Celestial Chemistry'', and he has published more than 160 scientific treatises. He was elected a Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1991.<ref name=Astronautix/>

== Space advocacy ==
As an expert in geological research on [[underground nuclear test]]s and [[extraterrestrial materials]], Ouyang was among the first to advocate not only the exploitation of [[Moon|lunar]] reserves of metals such as [[iron]], but also the mining of lunar [[helium-3]], an ideal fuel for [[nuclear fusion]] [[power plant]]s. Ouyang is now the chief scientist of the [[Chinese Lunar Exploration Program]] (CLEP), also known as the Chang'e program. He is the most prominent supporter of the Chinese crewed lunar exploration program, and also lobbies for the [[Chinese Mars exploration program|Chinese exploration of Mars]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/sports/2008-06/12/content_8352549.htm|script-title=zh:火炬手欧阳自远:“研究月球和举办奥运目标相通”|publisher=[[Xinhua]]|language=zh|date=June 12, 2008|access-date=October 22, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019225046/http://news.xinhuanet.com/sports/2008-06/12/content_8352549.htm|archive-date=October 19, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

On November 12, 2008, upon China's publication of a comprehensive lunar surface map, Ouyang encouraged all three Asian nations then involved in lunar exploration (China, [[India]] and [[Japan]]) to increase co-operation in furthering humanity's understanding of the Moon.<ref>[http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2008-11/12/content_10348521.htm "Chinese scientist calls for co-op between Asian space powers"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090303230504/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2008-11/12/content_10348521.htm |date=March 3, 2009 }}. Xinhua. November 12, 2008. Retrieved March 16, 2013.</ref>
